title: Briefing: France, Albania, India, Italy and South Africa
script: Good morning. It's Thursday, November fifth, and this is the Unowned briefing: the stories that matter, checked and graded. It's read by a synthetic voice, and every fact comes from our published timelines.
Every item carries our grade. Confirmed means independent outlets agree. Reported means one source so far. Disputed means the accounts conflict. And alleged is one side's claim.
Here are the top stories.
France. Today: Student, lycée and worker groups join inter‑syndical strike call for higher wages, public funding, wealth tax.
Albania. Yesterday: Democratic Party of Albania declares readiness for protests, demands Prime Minister Rama imprisoned.
India. Yesterday: Delhi government counsel consents to criminal contempt proceedings against Cockroach Janta Party legal head.
Italy. Yesterday: Rete degli Studenti Medi coordinator urges more school funding as students protest for teachers and themselves.
South Africa. Yesterday: South African Government says asylum seekers and refugees cannot vote under Refugee Regulations.
Canada. No new developments since Monday, November second.
Germany. No new developments since Monday, November second.
Serbia. No new developments since Monday, November second.
Now the details.

France. Today: Student, lycée and worker groups, among them the CFTC, Solidaires and CFE‑CGC, have joined the inter‑syndical call for a nationwide strike on 5 November, Le Monde reports. The strike call, initially issued by five employee unions, seeks higher wages, increased public‑service funding and a tax on large fortunes. Our grade: reported, from a single source so far.

Albania. Yesterday, Wednesday, November fourth: Democratic Party of Albania said in an Instagram post that it is ready for protests and calls for Prime Minister Rama to be imprisoned. That's their own claim, posted on their channel, and we grade it alleged.

India. Yesterday, Wednesday, November fourth: Delhi government counsel gave consent for criminal contempt proceedings against the Cockroach Janta Party's legal head over posts alleging a Saket court judge acted on outside orders, calling his view prima facie; the Delhi High Court will decide whether the case goes ahead, ETV Bharat reports. Our grade: reported. It rests on one source, ETV Bharat, and isn't yet confirmed by a second. Coming up: The Special Executive Magistrate hearing for the CJP leaders summoned over the Jantar Mantar protest listed for the third week of November.

Italy. Yesterday, Wednesday, November fourth: The national coordinator of the Rete degli Studenti Medi school-student network tells la Repubblica that the government should invest more in schools, and that fewer staff would lower the quality of teaching. Students say they are protesting for teachers as well as for themselves. We grade that reported: so far only la Repubblica has it, and we're waiting for independent confirmation. Coming up: Turnout and outcome of the CGIL general strike called for November twentieth.

South Africa. Yesterday, Wednesday, November fourth: The South African Government said on X, on local-election day, that asylum seekers and refugees may not vote. Its graphics cite the Refugee Regulations, which it says bar them from political activity, and the Electoral Act, which it says limits voting to registered citizens aged 18 or over. That's the authority's own claim, from its official statement, and we grade it alleged until independent reporting backs it up. Coming up: The new asylum appointment system Home Affairs said would be in place by November tenth.
Also on our watch, with no new developments in recent days.

Canada. The latest report, from Monday, November second: Nine British Columbia First Nations announce Federal Court applications to quash the Pacific Link national-interest designation, saying Ottawa did not adequately consult them. We grade that confirmed: independent outlets report it.

Germany. The latest report, from Monday, November second: Germany's Education Minister Karin Prien calls the concerns of the young people who marched in more than 30 cities on October thirty-first "legitimate and extremely relevant" and promises more dialogue, and SPD politicians call for a national education summit. Our grade: reported. It rests on one source, The Local Germany, and isn't yet confirmed by a second.

Serbia. The latest report, from Monday, November second: Serbia's Supreme Public Prosecutor's Office orders the Belgrade prosecutors to act on student complaints against criminal police chief Marko Kričak over an August 2025 incident in a Government of Serbia garage, which had gone more than a year without result, Vreme reports. We grade that reported: so far only Vreme has it, and we're waiting for independent confirmation.
We'll bring you updates on those as soon as they become available.

Coming up in the days ahead. Saturday, November fourteenth, Germany: Gen Z regelt plans another countrywide protest on November fourteenth. Sunday, November fifteenth, Canada: Whether binding Pathways carbon-storage agreements are signed by the November fifteenth target.
That's the Unowned briefing for Thursday, November fifth. Full timelines, and every source, are at unowned news dot com. Thanks for listening.
